Subject: Re: Intro + perf goals (FintechCo) — post-call recap

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and great clarity on the latency targets and residency requirements. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

- Goals you called out: 50–80ms median for inference in US regions, <100ms 95th; geo-fallback for EU with data residency guarantees for EU traffic.
- Primary blockers you mentioned: current vendor variability across regions, unclear SLA for cross-region failover, and higher per-token costs with your current hyperscaler setup.

What Redwood can do next:
- Run a short multi-region performance baseline (us-east1 / us-west1 / eu-west1) against your representative workload. We'll compare Redwood hosted API vs your current hyperscaler endpoints (you said AWS + GCP).
- Share a competitive brief that highlights where we differ (continuous batching, regional routing, prefix cache, and transparent per-token economics). Attached: Redwood-competitive-onepager.pdf.
- Clarify data residency options — Dedicated/Private deployment options and KMS integrations — see SOC2 summary we'll share.

Requested from you: a small sample prompt set (non-PII) we can use for the baseline and a short list of the three hyperscaler endpoints/regions you want compared.

Proposed timeline: baseline tests by EOD Thu (6/4), results & short write-up Mon (6/7), follow-up call Tues (6/8) to review results and outline a POC. 

Next steps (who does what):
- Alex: share sample prompt set + region endpoints by 6/2
- Marissa/Jordan: run baseline tests and share comparisons by 6/4
- Sean: prepare short SLO/cost model for comparison

Attachments: Redwood-competitive-onepager.pdf

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Jordan / Sean — please run the multi-region baseline per the plan below against the sample prompts Alex will drop in the shared folder. Keep everything reproducible (seed, model version, token limits).

Test plan (high level):
- Payload: Fintech-provided sample prompts (non-PII)
- Regions: us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1
- Comparators: Redwood hosted API (current stable), AWS endpoint (us-east1 / eu-west1), GCP endpoint (us-west1) — Alex provided endpoints in his email.
- Metrics: median latency, p95 latency, median tokens/sec, error rate, and tail latency during 1-minute bursts (50 RPS sustained, 200 RPS bursts).
- Deliverable: CSV with per-region rows + one-page summary of diffs and suggested mitigations (batching/kv cache/quantization).

Attach the test plan: redwood_test-plan.md. Jordan — can you run this by EOD 6/4? If you hit infra limits, please escalate and loop in Infra oncall.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-05T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: FintechCo — multi-region baseline plan (results)

Marissa / Sean — ran the baseline this morning. High-level results attached (redwood_multi-region-latency.csv). Summary: 

- Redwood hosted API (in our nearest gov/prod clusters)
  - us-east1: median 58ms, p95 95ms
  - us-west1: median 70ms, p95 120ms
  - eu-west1: median 85ms, p95 140ms

- Fintech-provided AWS endpoints (they looked to be standard endpoint configs)
  - us-east1: median 110ms, p95 180ms
  - eu-west1: median 160ms, p95 240ms

- Fintech-provided GCP endpoint (us-west1)
  - us-west1: median 130ms, p95 210ms

Notes/observations:
- Redwood maintained a consistent benefit in median latency across regions; advantage is larger in US regions because of our optimized serving runtime and regional edge routing.
- p95 gap narrows with increased batching on the comparator endpoints but introduces higher median in their tests; our continuous batching + KV cache keeps medians low while improving cost.
- EU tail latency still higher because of infrequent warm paths; recommend pre-warming or Dedicated capability in-region for production SLAs.

Attachments: redwood_multi-region-latency.csv

--
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex / Priya — sharing the baseline results Jordan ran (summary below) and next recommended steps. Full CSV and SLO table attached.

Quick summary:
- Median latency: Redwood hosted API ~60–85ms across regions vs 110–160ms for the hyperscaler endpoints Fintech provided.
- p95: Redwood 95–140ms, comparators 180–240ms; p95 gaps can be tightened with Dedicated/warmer routing in EU.
- Cost note: our continuous batching and prefix cache reduces per-token compute vs naive single-request models — we included a rough cost delta in the attached SLO_table.xlsx.

Why this matters: with Redwood you get predictable, regionalized latency plus deployment options (Hosted for fast POC, Dedicated/Private for contractual residency and tighter SLAs). For FintechCo's targets (50–80ms median; <100ms p95 in primary US regions), Hosted gets you close in US; Dedicated in EU recommended to meet tight contractual p95s and data residency requirements.

Proposed next steps:
- Live POC with regional routing & canary: 2-week POC using your sample prompts, Redwood hosted in US + Dedicated capacity in EU for residency. Proposed start: week of 6/15.
- Legal: we'll provision a data residency addendum and SOC2 appendix for review (I attached a redacted SOC2 earlier).
- Logistics: can we book a 30-minute sync on Tue 6/16 or Wed 6/17 to review the POC scope and success criteria?
